takeaway: A typical rainy-season Monday: a few showers along the coast early, then a partly cloudy morning, then scattered downpours with thunder this afternoon and some scattered rain on the peninsula tonight (Nicoya near 32°C). For surf, this morning is the pick of the week: the Caribbean trades are still blowing, so the wind is east to southeast, offshore to cross-offshore, on a solid 5–7 foot, 17-second south-southwest swell. The trades fade tonight. Tuesday starts light, then the wind goes onshore Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday look light from the north, which is better but not true offshore. The storm the hurricane center is watching will form well south of Mexico and head away from us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only. The window to keep an eye on has moved to about Oct 20–23, and the trades look set to return around Oct 17–22.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Mon–Wed, Oct 12–14)
periods.pattern: The band of tropical showers that sits over Central America this time of year is still over Costa Rica, but today's rain should be scattered rather than widespread. Costa Rica's weather service expects showers on the west-facing coasts early, scattered downpours with thunder on the North Pacific this afternoon, and scattered rain on the Nicoya Peninsula tonight. The heaviest rain is expected on the Central and South Pacific, not here. The Caribbean trades blow today, then fade tonight. Tuesday and Wednesday the wind goes light, and Pacific air takes over along our coast. In the models, the heaviest rain sits well offshore, south of Costa Rica and Panama, and Nicoya gets mostly light to moderate amounts.
periods.implications: Mornings are your outdoor window, though you may get an early coastal shower. Plan around afternoon storms each day. Today's should be hit-or-miss rather than a soaker. Highs stay around 31–33°C in Nicoya.
periods.confidence: High on decent mornings and afternoon storms. Moderate on how much rain any one afternoon brings to Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Thu–Sun, Oct 15–18)
periods.pattern: Light winds Thursday and Friday, then the easterly trades start rebuilding across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica over the weekend. The European AI ensemble brings them back as early as Friday. The European ensemble has them back by about Sunday. The U.S. ensemble also brings trades back over Nicaragua but keeps some southwest flow just south of Costa Rica. The weak low the models showed over Costa Rica for Oct 16–17 yesterday has mostly disappeared from today's runs. Rain in the model averages stays modest over Nicoya, and the wetter areas shift to the Caribbean side as the trades return.
periods.implications: Normal October days: good mornings, hit-or-miss afternoon storms. As the trades come back this weekend, the Pacific side should trend a bit drier and sunnier.
periods.confidence: Moderate on light winds Thursday and Friday and trades returning around the weekend. Moderate on mostly modest rain for Nosara.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Mon–Mon, Oct 19–26)
periods.pattern: The European and European AI ensembles keep easterly trades across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica from about Oct 18 to 22, with mostly light rain on Nicoya. The U.S. models are the wet outlier: their ensemble average has a broad band of heavier rain over the Pacific off Nicaragua and Costa Rica from about Oct 19 to 23, and the main U.S. model spins up a low off the Pacific coast of Nicaragua around Oct 20–22 that would pull moist southwest winds onto our coast. Costa Rica's long-range outlook still calls for below-normal rain: roughly 5–90 mm (up to about 3.5 inches) on the North Pacific for Oct 12–18, 1–70 mm for Oct 19–25, and very dry from about Oct 26.
periods.implications: Leans drier than a normal October, with offshore mornings likely around Oct 18–22. Keep Oct 20–23 a little flexible for anything rain-sensitive until the models settle.
periods.confidence: Moderate on trades returning around Oct 18–22. Low on the U.S. models' wetter scenario for Oct 20–23.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades this morning, offshore to cross-offshore at Nosara (east to southeast). They fade tonight. Tuesday starts light and variable, then Pacific flow takes over: southwest to west, onshore, Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are light north winds, side-shore. The trades should return around Oct 17–22.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:13 a.m. PDT Monday) has southeast 10–15 knots today, with moderate to fresh northeast to east winds in the Gulf of Papagayo itself. That's a little less east than yesterday's forecast, so think cross-offshore rather than straight offshore, and it may get side-on once the afternoon sea breeze kicks in. Tonight goes light and variable off Papagayo, with southeast to south 10–15 knots elsewhere. Tuesday is light and variable off Papagayo, southeast to south 10 knots elsewhere, turning southwest in the afternoon. Tuesday night and Wednesday are southwest to west 10 knots (onshore). Wednesday night is northwest 10. Thursday has north to northeast 10 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo and light winds elsewhere. Friday is north 10. Swell is south-southwest 5–7 feet at 17 seconds today and tonight, 16 seconds Tuesday, easing to 4–6 feet at 14 seconds Wednesday and Thursday, then a new long-period pulse at 16–17 seconds Thursday night and Friday. Nicaragua: the trades are blowing across Nicaragua today, so Nicaragua should be offshore most of the day. That's a good sign for a clean Nosara morning, but not all-day offshore here. All three ensembles bring those Nicaragua trades back between about Oct 16 and Oct 22.
surfWinds.bestWindows: This morning (Mon Oct 12) is the pick: offshore to cross-offshore with the biggest, longest-period swell of the week. Tuesday at dawn could be fair in light winds before it turns onshore. Wednesday looks onshore. Thursday and Friday mornings are light north wind, workable early, with a new long-period pulse arriving Friday. The next real offshore stretch looks like around Oct 18–22.
surfWinds.confidence: High on a clean-ish morning today. Moderate on onshore Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday. Moderate on trades returning around Oct 18–22.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established. Roughly the same level as yesterday, but the window to watch has moved later.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: About Oct 20–23, mainly in the U.S. models.
gyreWatch.supporting: The U.S. ensemble average shows a broad band of heavier rain over the Pacific off Nicaragua and Costa Rica from about Oct 19 to 23, with a heavy spot over southern Costa Rica around Oct 22. The main U.S. model develops a low off Nicaragua's Pacific coast around Oct 20–22 with southwest winds feeding our coast, which is the kind of setup that brings multi-day Pacific rain. The European AI ensemble also shows a weak low near the Gulf of Fonseca around Oct 22. The U.S. tropics outlook (Oct 6) gives low odds of a storm forming in the far eastern Pacific in that late-October window.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The European and European AI ensembles bring easterly trades back across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica from about Oct 16–18 through Oct 22, which usually keeps the Pacific side drier, and they keep Nicoya's rain mostly light. Yesterday's weak low over Costa Rica for Oct 16–17 has mostly faded from today's runs. The storm the hurricane center is watching (90% within a week) forms well south of southern Mexico and moves west-northwest, away from us. Costa Rica's weather service expects no extreme events Oct 12–18 and below-normal rain through Oct 25, turning very dry on the North Pacific from about Oct 26. The U.S. tropics outlook expects below-normal Caribbean rain and doesn't flag a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: Today's marine forecast has southeast winds this morning instead of east, so it's cross-offshore rather than straight offshore, and the trades fade tonight instead of Monday afternoon. Tuesday is now light and variable turning southwest, rather than a light north wind. Thursday and Friday now show light north to northeast winds instead of west to northwest, which is better for surf, and a new long-period pulse shows up Friday. Nicoya's high is about 32°C (yesterday 33°C), and Costa Rica's weather service calls today's rain scattered. The hurricane center's system is now 80% in two days and 90% in a week (from 20% and 80%), still far to the west and heading away. The weak low over Costa Rica for Oct 16–17 has mostly faded, so that watch window is gone. A new, lower-confidence one shows up around Oct 20–23 in the U.S. models only. The trades' return looks a bit earlier, around Oct 17–22 instead of Oct 19–23.
practical: Surf this morning: it's the cleanest wind and best swell of the week. Get outside in the mornings and expect hit-or-miss afternoon storms. Tuesday dawn is your next best surf bet, then go very early or skip Wednesday. Thursday and Friday mornings are workable in light north winds. Keep Oct 20–23 a bit flexible. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
